title: Subtitle Ladder
user: Independent spoken-language learners who want repeatable listening-and-speaking practice that gradually removes translation support.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A learner seeking conversational German receives advice to use comprehensible input and a step-down sequence from target-audio/English subtitles to target subtitles to no subtitles.
AnkiDroid's current custom-study-by-tags UX work demonstrates that learners need narrower study subsets rather than one undifferentiated review queue.

recurrence: A direct 2025 spoken-language request and a 2025 study-subset UX issue both point to the need to control difficulty and scope deliberately.
current_workaround: Rewatch videos while manually changing subtitle settings, save timestamps in notes, or make separate decks by difficulty.
incumbents_and_gap: Language Reactor and streaming subtitles help consume media; Anki schedules words. Neither is a local, repeatable ladder for a learner's own short licensed/public-domain clips and recordings.
smallest_useful_product: A PWA that accepts user-recorded or public-domain audio plus a caption file, creates 15–60 second loops, and offers translation, target-text, masked-word, and no-text stages with a spoken self-recording.
success_measure: Half of pilots complete the same clip in three support levels and make at least five self-recordings in two weeks.
constraints: Only user-owned, licensed, or public-domain media; keep recordings local; captions require Unicode/RTL support; no fluency claims.
why_distinct: It operationalizes a gradual support-removal practice routine rather than providing another course or subtitle browser extension.
